jobs.title: Peer Support Specialist Apprentice – Department of Public Health & Environment
jobs.description:
**About Our Job**
=================

  

With competitive pay, great benefits, and endless opportunities, working for the City and County of Denver means seeing yourself working with purpose — for you, and those who benefit from your passion, skills and expertise. Join our diverse, inclusive and talented workforce of more than 11,000 team members who are at the heart of what makes Denver, Denver.

**What We Offer**
-----------------


The City and County of Denver offers a competitive salary commensurate with education and experience. The salary range for this position is $23\.89\. We also offer generous benefits for full\-time employees which include but are not limited to:

* A guaranteed life\-long monthly pension, once vested after 5 years of service
* 457B Retirement Plan
* 140 hours of PTO earned within first year \+ 12 paid holidays, 1 personal holiday, 1 Wellness Day and 1 volunteer day per year
* Competitive medical, dental and vision plans effective within 1 month of start date

 ***This is a limited position with an end date of one year from date of hire.***

**Location**
------------


The City and County of Denver supports a hybrid workplace model. Employees are expected to work on\-site at their designated job location at least three (3\) days per week, with off\-site work permitted as needed. Employees must perform all off\-site work within the state of Colorado. Hybrid schedule is determined by individual departments and teams and may be subject to change in order to meet the needs and capacity.

**What You’ll Do**
------------------


Denver's Department of Public Health \& Environment (DDPHE) is dedicated to advancing Denver's environmental and public health goals. DDPHE works collaboratively with city, state and community partners to conduct education, community engagement, and enforcement to promote healthy people, healthy pets, and a sustainable environment. DDPHE oversees a number of services related to public health and the environment and is comprised of seven divisions: Division of Shared Services and Business Operations; Community \& Behavioral Health; Public Health Investigations; Denver Animal Protection; the Office of Medical Examiner; Emergency Management and Medical Operations; and Environmental Quality. For more information on DDPHE’s programs and services, visit the DDPHE website at: Denver Department of Public Health \& Environment.

 ***We foster an inclusive culture by respecting the values, customs, and authenticity of everyone and by implementing equitable public health strategies so Denver communities can thrive.***

  

DDPHE is building a more representative workforce that reflects the diversity of Denver communities. We have two **Peer Support Specialist Apprentice** positions available for those interested in exploring a career in public and/or environmental health, public safety and community support. Peer Support Specialists with the City and County of Denver play an important role in building a more representative and inclusive public health and safety workforce that reflects the diverse communities of Denver. Peer Support Specialists use their lived experience, relationship\-building skills, and knowledge of community resources to connect individuals with support, services, and opportunities that promote health and well\-being. Prior training and certificates are not needed for this apprenticeship program. Specific requirements are to be completed within the 1\-year on\-the\-job training period.

  

Specifically, in this role, you will:

* Build person\-centered, trauma\-informed relationships with clients using a peer support model.
* Apply Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration’s (SAMHSA) Core Competencies for Peer Workers and National Practice Standards for Peer Supporters to deliver recovery\-oriented, person\-centered, voluntary, and relationship\-focused services.
* Collaborate with multidisciplinary City and County staff, including administrative professionals, paralegals, attorneys, nurses, outreach workers and other team members, to provide holistic, client\-centered support.
* Leverage lived experience to foster hope and connect clients with recovery, behavioral health, community resources, and supportive services.
* Partner with clients to establish self\-directed goals, identify resources and service needs, develop action plans, and monitor progress toward desired outcomes.
* Support community members by developing individualized support plans, and facilitating connections to community resources
* Coordinate and facilitate access to services by assisting clients with phone calls, accompanying them to court and community appointments, and navigating multiple service systems.
* Maintain accurate, timely documentation of client interactions, progress, and other activities in accordance with organizational standards.
* Complete DDPHE 60 hours Colorado Peer and Family Specialist (CPFS) training curriculum
* Pass CPFS exam and receive certification
* Participate and complete Colorado School of Public Health micro\-credentialling program
* Other duties as needed and assigned

 **These positions will rotate to two of five** **divisions/departments** **within the City and County of Denver for 6\-month terms. See information below about each division.**

* **Office of the Municipal Public Defender****:** OMPD’s Client Support Team (CST) consists of four Peer Support Specialists, a Behavioral Health Navigator, and a Bilingual Outreach Case Coordinator who work alongside attorneys in court daily, create re\-entry plans with clients in jail, and connect clients with resources like shelter/housing, benefit enrollment, behavioral health treatment, and more. The CST division serves as part of the defense team and is bound by the Colorado Rules of Professional Conduct including rules regarding attorney\-client privilege and client confidentiality.

Those values represent the touchstone for the organization, guiding the decisions of the individuals and the organization. * Make a difference in the lives of real people every day

The Water Environmental Inspection Supervisor is responsible for ensuring environmental inspections surrounding wastewater and stormwater are completed and meet regulatory requirements stipulated in permits and other associated programs. The position is also responsible for supervision of inspection staff and ensuring completion of work duties and assignments.

* Identifies and evaluates environmental program needs and implements select environmental programs
* Prepares reports and correspondence on matters related to programs for City, State and Federal agencies

* Supervises field inspectors
* Provides technical support to management and operating departments
* Develops and conducts public outreach and educational activities on City programs or environmental issues
* Responds to hazardous and non\-hazardous material spills and incidents
* Responds to citizen complaints or inquiries
* Assists in developing operational priorities, goals and objectives
* Develops and implements work procedures and policies
* Supervises, evaluates, trains and instructs assigned employees
* Prepares and monitors program budget, including expenditures
* Coordinates compliance and enforcement activities with code enforcement
* Makes recommendations regarding selection, hiring, training, evaluating, and disciplining of assigned employees
* Performs additional duties as assigned

 **MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS \& WORKING CONDITIONS**


An equivalent combination of education, training, and experience that demonstrates required knowledge, skills, and abilities may be considered.

 **Education:**

  

* Bachelor's Degree in Environmental Science, Construction Management, Hydrology, Geology, Biology or closely related field

 **Experience:**

  

* At least 6 years progressively responsible experience in wastewater pretreatment, stormwater conveyance systems and their design, and environmental compliance related to construction site stormwater management.

 **Licenses and Certifications:**

  

* Colorado Driver's License with a good driving history;
* HAZWOPER 40\-Hour Certification;
* NIMS 100 training; and
* NIMS 700 training.

 **Preferred** **Qualifications:**

  

* 2 years of experience as a lead worker or direct supervisory experience
* At least 2 years of MS4 Program management experience
* At least 2 years of experience developing SOP’s and improving existing processes

 **Knowledge:**

  

* Comprehensive knowledge of federal, state and local environmental regulations as they relate to wastewater and stormwater;
* Comprehensive knowledge of the principles and practices related to general construction practices, stormwater conveyance systems, sewer collection systems and other public infrastructure;
* Knowledge of spill response protocols and HAZWOPER standards and procedures;
* Comprehensive understanding of inspection methods and associated enforcement measures;
* Understanding of stormwater management plan design; and
* Knowledge of construction site best management practices used to control the transport of pollutants through stormwater.

* Ability to perform mathematical calculations;
* Ability to write, maintain and review detailed reports, logs, and inspection records;

**Pay \& FSLA Status:** Competitive Compensation, D.O.E.; Hourly non\-exempt

**Regular Schedule \& Shift:** Monday – Friday, Day Shift

**Regular Weekly Hours:** Full\-time/40 hours per week (overtime as needed)


**Management Position:** No

**POSITION SUMMARY:**


The Warehouse Supervisor is responsible for providing daily direction and assignments for warehouse team members. Our warehouse team is responsible for the daily receiving, scanning, pulling, picking, and order building to meet and exceed customer demand and expectations. Through safe behaviors, the Warehouse Supervisor will work alongside their team to meet the established productivity goals. This position will work directly with their immediate supervisor and have significant influence in all areas regarding staffing, employee engagement and development, and accountability. This is a labor\-intensive position that requires heavy lifting. Individuals are regularly on their feet throughout the day and may work at heights as required. Safety is a priority.

Join our diverse, inclusive and talented workforce of more than 11,000 team members who are at the heart of what makes Denver, Denver.

 **What We Offer**


The City and County of Denver offers a competitive salary commensurate with education and experience. The salary range for this position is $23\.89 \- $29\.86\. We also offer generous benefits for full\-time employees which include but are not limited to:

* A guaranteed life\-long monthly pension, once vested after 5 years of service
* 457B Retirement Plan
* 140 hours of PTO earned within first year \+ 12 paid holidays, 1 personal holiday, 1 Wellness Day and 1 volunteer day per year
* Competitive medical, dental and vision plans effective within 1 month of start date

 **Location**


The City and County of Denver supports a hybrid workplace model. In this position, you can expect to work mostly in the field, and within the office when needed. The office for this position is located at 201 W. Colfax Ave., Denver, CO 80202\.

 **What You’ll Do**


Denver's Department of Public Health and Environment (DDPHE) is dedicated to advancing Denver's environmental and public health goals. DDPHE works collaboratively with city, state and community partners to conduct education, community engagement, and enforcement to promote healthy people, healthy pets, and a sustainable environment. DDPHE oversees a number of services related to public health and the environment and is comprised of seven divisions: Division of Shared Services and Business Operations; Community \& Behavioral Health; Public Health Investigations; Denver Animal Protection; the Office of Medical Examiner; Emergency Management and Medical Operations, and Environmental Quality. For more information on DDPHE’s programs and services, visit the DDPHE website at: Denver Department of Public Health and Environment.

 ***We foster an inclusive culture by respecting the values, customs, and authenticity of everyone and by implementing equitable public health strategies so Denver communities can thrive.***

  

As the **Peer Support Specialist I** you will be a dedicated and experienced individual to serve on the Focus Area Street Engagement Team. This team provides direct services to a diverse group of people, where they are, by way of outreach, in the community. We work collaboratively with people from various backgrounds and experiences; and people who often experience trauma, stigma and oppression, including: people who use substances, people living with mental health challenges, and people experiencing unstable housing. This position will work in ever changing environments, and exposed to the seasonal elements of Denver. A majority of the work is completed outside of an office setting, in compact spaces, and on foot.

  

Specifically, as the Peer Support Specialist I you will:

* Work daily within a geographic area prioritized for outreach to connect people to shelter, housing, and other services.
* Collaborate closely with multidisciplinary outreach team to develop daily operational plan focusing on unique demographics, service needs, and other special considerations.
* Approach individuals on the street in the Focus Area. Engage individuals in trauma\-responsive and person\-focused interactions
* Leverage lived experience and core competencies in Peer Support to cultivate meaningful, authentic relationships grounded in mutual respect and collaboration.
* Engage individuals with goal setting methods to identify services, resources, partners, and develop timelines to succeed in self\-determined goals.
* Provide support for resource navigation to those seeking services
* Complete warm hand\-offs, including transporting individuals to their next destination
* Ensure vehicle is fully stocked with supplies necessary for successful operations
* Provide comprehensive support and accuracy in relation to data needs and collection
* Maintain documentation standards in recording daily activities and interactions
* Research and operationalize best practices of peer support and peer navigation services to inform work.
* Create and foster professional relationships with networks and organizations.
* Along with all DDPHE staff, actively participate in emergency preparedness and response team activities to support DDPHE’s responsibilities outlined in the City’s Emergency Operations Plan. This may require being ‘on\-call’ from time to time respond to emergencies. Training will be provided.
* Other duties as assigned.

 **What You’ll Bring**


We value diversity of ethnicity, race, socioeconomic status, sexual identity, gender, religion, language, ability, and experience and exemplify this through the makeup of our team at all levels. You'll be right at home here if you cultivate strong relationships and push yourself, your work, the people around you and Denver to the next level.

* Two (2\) years of lived experience with significant mental health and or substance misuse challenges

jobs.title: Board-Certified Behavior Analyst - Clinical Supervisor
jobs.description:
**Board\-Certified Behavior Analyst \- Clinical Supervisor Teens \& Young Adults (Ages 12–21\)** 

**M–F 8–4 \| 7 Weeks Paid Time Off \| Arvada, CO**

**Salary: $75,000 – $86,700/year** 

**Full\-time \| Center\-based, no in\-home travel**

**A BCBA role with a school\-year rhythm**

Most BCBA jobs ask for evenings, weekends, and hours in the car between client homes. This one doesn't. You'll work Monday through Friday, 8:00 AM to 4:00 PM, in one building, with **up to 7 weeks of paid time off every year**. That includes 5 weeks of paid center closures: a week in spring, a week in summer, Thanksgiving week, and up to two weeks over the winter holidays. That's on top of your PTO, sick leave, and paid holidays.

**Who we are**

Evoke Behavioral Health is a **locally owned** Colorado organization serving individuals with autism, intellectual and developmental disabilities, and co\-occurring diagnoses. In 2025 we moved into a **newly renovated** facility in Arvada with two outdoor playgrounds, a full gym, and an advanced sensory room.

You won't be working alone. Our team includes BCBAs, LCSWs, special education teachers, RBTs, and mental health assistants, plus on\-site nursing, HR, admin, and maintenance staff. When a situation escalates or a case gets complicated, the right people are down the hall.

**What you'll do**

You'll serve as clinical lead for individuals in our **Secondary/Transition Program**, a population where behavior analysis can change what adulthood looks like: independence, vocational skills, and communication that works outside the classroom.

* Conduct assessments and design individualized treatment plans for teens and young adults
* Lead a team of approximately 6\-7 RBTs and Behavior Specialists (about 800–1,000 RBT hours per month), providing supervision and training
* Supervise BCBA trainees and help grow the next generation of clinicians
* Partner with families through caregiver training and collaborate with our interdisciplinary team
* Use data to guide clinical decisions and keep documentation current
* Provide in\-the\-moment clinical support, including Safety Care when needed

**What you bring**

* Active BCBA certification in good standing
* 2\+ years as a BCBA, experience with adolescents, high\-intensity behavior, co\-occurring diagnoses, interdisciplinary teams, preffered
* Master's degree in ABA, Psychology, Special Education, or a related field
* Experience training and supervising behavior technicians
* Experience working with individuals with autism and/or developmental disabilities
* Ability to pass state and federal background checks
* CPR/First Aid certification (can be obtained within 30 days of hire)
* Ability to physically participate in Safety Care, including kneeling, moving quickly, and lifting up to 40 lbs.

**Benefits**

* **Up to 7 weeks paid time off:** 5 weeks of paid center closures, 7 paid holidays, 40 hours PTO, 48 hours sick leave
* Medical, dental, and vision insurance, plus an HSA with eligible plan
* 401(k) with up to 3% company match
* Internal and external CEU opportunities

Openings as of 9/25/2026

  

Campus Security Supervisor \- High School
JobID: 10607  

* + Position Type:  
	
	 School Based Support: Secretary, Para, Custodian/Campus Security
	+ Date Posted:  
	
	 9/24/2026
	+ Location:  
	
	 Prairie View High School
	+ Date Available:  
	
	 October 2026
	+ Closing Date:
	  
	
	 09/30/2026  

**DESCRIPTION:** Insure the high school campus and building is safe and efficient by patrolling the building and grounds, monitoring student behavior, diffusing hostile situations, monitoring traffic in student parking lot, assisting administration and counselors with counseling, enforcing school rules, and providing for the overall security of students.  

  

**SALARY:** Classified Grade N, starting at $23\.20 per hour to start, depending on recent relevant experience. 10 hours per day on the 158 day, 9\-month work schedule. Position is paid over 12\-months and is eligible for benefits.  

  

**DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:**


	+ Monitor campus, parking lots, lunch areas, and high school building to prevent property damage, provide security, and regulate unauthorized persons from being on campus. Do timely perimeters checks of campus.
	+ Maintain camera systems, installing, monitoring and burning videos.
	+ Mediate student conflicts, Investigate drug and alcohol cases, complete student searches and communicate with SRO's when needed. Monitor students in order to eliminate truancy and to prevent physical altercations, disagreements, and drug and alcohol use on campus. Assist teachers with disruptive students and assist admin in front office security. Implement and enforce attendance policy and dress code.
	+ Supervise drills.
	+ Supervise evening events: games, dances, school events, prom, graduation. Assist with event set up if needed. **QUALIFICATIONS:**


	+ High school diploma or equivalent
	+ Specialized courses in law enforcement and/or security preferred.
	+ Strong interpersonal and communication skills.
	+ Desire to work with at\-risk youth.
	+ Knowledge of and experience in law enforcement.
	+ Ability to make effective decisions while dealing with ambiguous situations.
	+ Operating knowledge of and experience with computers, telephone, and two\-way radio.
	+ Must occasionally lift and/or move up to 50 pounds.
	+ Must be able to pass a Colorado and Federal Bureau of Investigation background check. **REQUIRED EXPERIENCE:**


	+ Over two years and up to three years' experience working with at\-risk youth, some in law enforcement or security.
	+ Basic math, accounting and English skills.
	+ Intermediate oral and written communication; interpersonal relations; personal computer; keyboarding and work processing skills and organizational skills.
	+ Advanced customer service and public relations skills, critical thinking and problem solving skills.
	+ The ability to manage confidentiality in all aspects of job, manage multiple priorities, manage multiple tasks with frequent interruptions, and ability to diffuse and manage volatile and stressful situations.
	+ Bilingual in Spanish preferred.  

  

All future correspondence will be handled via the email address you provided in your online application. Check your In\-Box and your SPAM folder.

jobs.title: GROUP SUPERVISOR
jobs.description:
✨Join a group of passionate advocates on our mission to improve the lives of youth! Rite of Passage Team is hiring for a Group Supervisor at Mt. Evans Qualifying House in Idaho Springs, CO ✨



The Colorado Qualifying House (Q House) is a transitional housing \& positive skill development program located on over 70 acres of land at the bottom of Mt. Blue Sky. The Q house serves as a Residential Treatment Center that provides male youth ages 16\-21 with opportunities for positive growth through evidence\-based interventions and innovative programming, including on\-site school \& vocational opportunities, therapeutic support, community engagement, and tailored programming that is co\-created in collaboration with all youth and staff.



The Q House program subscribes to the four principles of effective intervention: risk assessment, addressing needs, providing individualized treatment, and ensuring fidelity. By following these core principles, Colorado Qualifying House supports youth in developing the skills and resources necessary to lead self\-determined lives without experiencing the barriers of future systems involvement. Our trauma\-informed approach emphasizes collaborative growth and recognizes that every person – staff and youth alike – has goals that we can collectively use our knowledge and experiences to mutually support.


**Pay:** $55,000 annually  

  

**Perks \& Benefits:**


* 3\.5 day work weeks (Sunday\-Tuesday 7am\-7pm, Wednesday 7am\-3pm)
* Optional on\-site housing to ease travel during your shift days if desired
* Free shift meals and snacks (tell us what you’d like!)
* Medical, Dental, Vision and company paid Life Insurance within 90 days
* 401k match of up to 6% after 1 year of employment,
* Paid Time Off that can be used as soon as it accrues
* Tuition Reimbursement Options
* Hiring preference for future leadership \& career development opportunities
* And more here: ROP\-benefits\-and\-perks\-2 (https://riteofpassage.com/wp\-content/uploads/2024/10/ROP\-benefits\-perks\-2024\-v2\.pdf)

  

  

**What you will do:**



The Group Supervisor facilitates collaboration among staff and youth to ensure all expectations of the program and its services are met. They will assess the day’s needs and work with the team to identify leads for each task, and ensure completion according to the specifications required by licensing and shown to have the greatest success in implementation. This includes the morning cadence (wake up, chores, physical education), participating in work, school, or community service, and the evening cadence (dinner, positive skill development groups, and leisure time before bed). We strongly believe in the importance of Continuous Quality Improvement, and are looking for an active partner eager to help the site find the best methods and approaches for exceeding our goals – as staff, youth, and the program as a whole.



This Group Supervisor will work on A Shift (Sunday – Wednesday afternoon) and have a Coach Counselor and Night Coach Counselor as direct reports. All on\-site staff (including the Teacher, Program Manager, and other support staff throughout the day) are charged with the safety, care, and around\-the\-clock supervision of students in the program. Most of the time the Group Supervisor will be at the Qualifying House in Idaho Springs, with consistent community outings in Clear Creek County and the greater Denver Metro area (volunteering with the local Elks Lodge, going to museums, hikes \& ski trips, etc). This role will work with the team to make sure regardless of location or programming (at the house, working in community, going on field trips) there is active supervision and support provided to the youth according to licensing requirements and in line with student needs.



“Kids with trauma history don’t need more punishment; and – quite frankly – they don’t need more stickers” \- Dr. Ross Greene



“I went to the woods because I wished to live deliberately, to front only the essentials facts of life, and see if I could not learn what it had to teach, and not, when I came to die, discover that I had not lived.” \- Henry David Thoreau


**Minimum Qualifications:**


* Have direct care experience working with at\-risk youth and/or the systems they frequently interact with
* Be empathetic, trauma\-informed, and able to model the positive impact of building healthy relationships
* Have experience in a supervisory role.
* Be at least 21 years of age.
* Have a high school diploma or equivalent.
* Be able to pass a criminal background check, illegal drug screen, physical, and TB test.
* The ability to work 3\.5 days/week in Idaho Springs (preference given to candidates in the greater Denver Metro area)
* Have reliable transportation and able to drive in winter conditions


**Applicants that stand out may:**


* Have a BA/BS in Human Services or related fields, or are actively working towards one
* Have lived experience that mirrors some of the lives of our students (navigating state systems, foster care, incarceration, or poverty support programs)
* Have previous experience with or knowledge of ACEs, trauma\-informed care, peer support, and other related research \& methodologies


After 40 years of improving the lives of youth, we are looking for passionate advocates to continue the legacy of helping young people become successful adults. As a Group Supervisor**,** you will have the unique opportunity to create a positive, safe and supportive environment for the youth we serve while building a career rich in growth opportunities and self\-fulfillment.

jobs.title: Certified Diabetes Care and Education Specialist
jobs.description:
We save lives while providing the opportunity for people to realize their healthy selves.:
**Certified Diabetes Care and Education Specialist****Monte Nido****1099 Contract role/Remote** **Monte Nido has been delivering treatment for eating disorders for over two decades.** Our programs offer a model of treatment that blends medically sophisticated care with a personalized treatment approach. Our work is grounded in evidence\-based strategies for adults and adolescents suffering from eating disorders. We work from a multi\-disciplinary treatment team approach while integrating state\-of\-the\-art medical, psychiatric, nutritional, and clinical strategies to provide comprehensive care within an intimate home setting.  

Under direction of the VP of Adolescent Medicine the Certified Diabetes Care and Education Specialist (CDCES) acts as an interface between client, home team, and medical team to guide optimal diabetes care while in treatment at Monte Nido. CDCES will guide insulin and other medication management in direct coordination with medical team, as well as the rest of the care team in reviewing glucometer readings, optimizing diabetes management, and educating patients on any lifestyle changes recommended. The employee is responsible for establishing and maintaining interpersonal relationships with patients, family, home team, and staff in a courteous, respectful, and professional manner to facilitate optimal care.  

This is a contract remote position working 8\-15 hours/week, census dependent.  

\#LI\-REMOTE  


Total Rewards::  

We are committed to creating a diverse environment and are proud to be an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, genetics, disability, age, or veteran status.
Responsibilities Include::
* Serves as Quality Coordinator, providing oversight of Diabetes Self\-Management Education and Support MNA services, ensuring:
	+ Implementation of the standards
	+ Services are evidence\-based.
	+ Service design incorporates population needs.
	+ Ongoing service evaluation and continuous quality improvement plan is reviewed at least annually.
	+ Collection and evaluation of data to identify gaps in services
	+ Keeping up to date with most current interventions and devices
* Educates patients on necessary lifestyle changes involved in diabetes diagnosis and management, including nutrition, blood glucose levels, medications/insulin, or pump management when prescribed by medical staff.
* If the sole role is diabetes management, collaborate with other assigned disciplines. Work with RD in the management of meal plans and physical activity. Work with the medical team in the management of blood sugars and medication changes.
* Performs data collection if needed to use for assessment and patient management (i.e., blood sugar monitoring /monitoring of CGMs)
* Facilitate diabetes and nutrition education classes.
* Provide family support as needed.
* Provide in\-service training to MNA departments as needed.
* Maintains a library of accurate and appropriate education materials as an adjunct to counseling and education.
* Demonstrates ability to document in the patient record in an accurate, concise, clear, legible, and organized manner that reflects assessment, interventions, and plans.
* Ability to dine with patients as scheduled.
* Participate in staff meetings when asked; responsible for obtaining information if not in attendance.
* Participates in committees as directed by the supervisor.
* Seeking out learning experiences and incorporating new knowledge into practice by attending and/or presenting at local and national conferences as approved and when opportunities arise.
* Responds and assists in emergency situations as needed in a manner appropriate to training and experience.
* Approaches patients/families/professionals and visitors with a respectful, caring manner to convey a sense of professionalism, concern, and warmth.
* Maintains confidentiality of patient information and records.
* Communicates and problem\-solves collaboratively with all team members.
* Delivers care in a non\-judgmental and non\-discriminatory manner, sensitive to patient diversity.
* Seeks constructive criticism and has the ability to evaluate suggestions objectively.
* Attends in\-services and educational training as necessary.
* Maintains flexibility and adaptability to expected or unexpected changes in the work environment.
* Reports incident occurrences in accordance with policy and procedure.
* In an emergency or declared state of emergency, may be required to stay connected virtually to help with urgent concerns.
* Performs all other tasks as assigned


Qualifications::
* Graduation from an accredited college or university with a minimum of a Bachelor’s Degree in Nutrition or a related field of human services.
* Three years of Clinical experience preferred
* Experience facilitating behavior change in the area of eating disorders/mental health preferred
* Certified Diabetes Care and Education Specialist Credential
* Registered Dietitian or a Registered Nurse
* CPR certification may be required based on state regulations.
* Knowledge of the Principles and Practices of the discipline.
* Knowledge of nutritional sciences and current treatments for diabetes and related manifestations
* Experience giving presentations and facilitating group classes
* Skilled use of Electronic Medical Records
* Ability to work both independently and in a team environment

new_jobs.description:
**About Our Job**
=================

  

With competitive pay, great benefits, and endless opportunities, working for the City and County of Denver means seeing yourself working with purpose — for you, and those who benefit from your passion, skills and expertise. Join our diverse, inclusive and talented workforce of more than 11,000 team members who are at the heart of what makes Denver, Denver.

**What We Offer**
-----------------


The City and County of Denver offers a competitive salary commensurate with education and experience. The salary range for this position is $23\.89\. We also offer generous benefits for full\-time employees which include but are not limited to:

* A guaranteed life\-long monthly pension, once vested after 5 years of service
* 457B Retirement Plan
* 140 hours of PTO earned within first year \+ 12 paid holidays, 1 personal holiday, 1 Wellness Day and 1 volunteer day per year
* Competitive medical, dental and vision plans effective within 1 month of start date

 ***This is a limited position with an end date of one year from date of hire.***

**Location**
------------


The City and County of Denver supports a hybrid workplace model. Employees are expected to work on\-site at their designated job location at least three (3\) days per week, with off\-site work permitted as needed. Employees must perform all off\-site work within the state of Colorado. Hybrid schedule is determined by individual departments and teams and may be subject to change in order to meet the needs and capacity.

**What You’ll Do**
------------------


Denver's Department of Public Health \& Environment (DDPHE) is dedicated to advancing Denver's environmental and public health goals. DDPHE works collaboratively with city, state and community partners to conduct education, community engagement, and enforcement to promote healthy people, healthy pets, and a sustainable environment. DDPHE oversees a number of services related to public health and the environment and is comprised of seven divisions: Division of Shared Services and Business Operations; Community \& Behavioral Health; Public Health Investigations; Denver Animal Protection; the Office of Medical Examiner; Emergency Management and Medical Operations; and Environmental Quality. For more information on DDPHE’s programs and services, visit the DDPHE website at: Denver Department of Public Health \& Environment.

 ***We foster an inclusive culture by respecting the values, customs, and authenticity of everyone and by implementing equitable public health strategies so Denver communities can thrive.***

  

DDPHE is building a more representative workforce that reflects the diversity of Denver communities. We have two **Peer Support Specialist Apprentice** positions available for those interested in exploring a career in public and/or environmental health, public safety and community support. Peer Support Specialists with the City and County of Denver play an important role in building a more representative and inclusive public health and safety workforce that reflects the diverse communities of Denver. Peer Support Specialists use their lived experience, relationship\-building skills, and knowledge of community resources to connect individuals with support, services, and opportunities that promote health and well\-being. Prior training and certificates are not needed for this apprenticeship program. Specific requirements are to be completed within the 1\-year on\-the\-job training period.

  

Specifically, in this role, you will:

* Build person\-centered, trauma\-informed relationships with clients using a peer support model.
* Apply Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration’s (SAMHSA) Core Competencies for Peer Workers and National Practice Standards for Peer Supporters to deliver recovery\-oriented, person\-centered, voluntary, and relationship\-focused services.
* Collaborate with multidisciplinary City and County staff, including administrative professionals, paralegals, attorneys, nurses, outreach workers and other team members, to provide holistic, client\-centered support.
* Leverage lived experience to foster hope and connect clients with recovery, behavioral health, community resources, and supportive services.
* Partner with clients to establish self\-directed goals, identify resources and service needs, develop action plans, and monitor progress toward desired outcomes.
* Support community members by developing individualized support plans, and facilitating connections to community resources
* Coordinate and facilitate access to services by assisting clients with phone calls, accompanying them to court and community appointments, and navigating multiple service systems.
* Maintain accurate, timely documentation of client interactions, progress, and other activities in accordance with organizational standards.
* Complete DDPHE 60 hours Colorado Peer and Family Specialist (CPFS) training curriculum
* Pass CPFS exam and receive certification
* Participate and complete Colorado School of Public Health micro\-credentialling program
* Other duties as needed and assigned

* **Office of the Municipal Public Defender****:** OMPD’s Client Support Team (CST) consists of four Peer Support Specialists, a Behavioral Health Navigator, and a Bilingual Outreach Case Coordinator who work alongside attorneys in court daily, create re\-entry plans with clients in jail, and connect clients with resources like shelter/housing, benefit enrollment, behavioral health treatment, and more. This position will work in ever changing environments, and exposed to the seasonal elements of Denver. A majority of the work is completed outside of an office setting, in compact spaces, and on foot.

* Collaborate closely with multidisciplinary outreach team to develop daily operational plan focusing on unique demographics, service needs, and other special considerations.
* Approach individuals on the street in the Focus Area. Engage individuals in trauma\-responsive and person\-focused interactions

* Provide support for resource navigation to those seeking services
* Complete warm hand\-offs, including transporting individuals to their next destination
* Ensure vehicle is fully stocked with supplies necessary for successful operations
* Provide comprehensive support and accuracy in relation to data needs and collection
* Maintain documentation standards in recording daily activities and interactions
* Research and operationalize best practices of peer support and peer navigation services to inform work.
* Create and foster professional relationships with networks and organizations.
* Along with all DDPHE staff, actively participate in emergency preparedness and response team activities to support DDPHE’s responsibilities outlined in the City’s Emergency Operations Plan. This may require being ‘on\-call’ from time to time respond to emergencies. Training will be provided.
* Other duties as assigned.

We value diversity of ethnicity, race, socioeconomic status, sexual identity, gender, religion, language, ability, and experience and exemplify this through the makeup of our team at all levels. You'll be right at home here if you cultivate strong relationships and push yourself, your work, the people around you and Denver to the next level.

  

Our ideal candidate has some or all the following experience, skills, and characteristics:


* Two (2\) years of lived experience with significant mental health and or substance misuse challenges
* Two (2\) years of delivering peer support services
* At least one (1\) year of working with unhoused community members, individuals with problematic substance use, and individuals diagnosed with a severe and persistent mental illness, and/or engaging in street outreach
* Bi\-cultural, bi\-lingual, and/or culturally sensitive; cross\-cultural skills, and experience with culturally diverse populations and demonstrated commitment and ability to advance diversity and inclusion.
* Knowledge of Harm reduction strategies and principles.
* Peer and Family Specialist certification approved by Colorado Providers Association (COPA)
